This is the documentation for [[Template:Card]], the card-page template.

One page = one printing. Do '''not''' put empty errata sections on a card that was never errata'd.

Optional '''card_status''' — a short status label for a printing that needs context outside the standard Decipher / Players Committee bands (for example, a cancelled design's community remaster). The label appears above the card template. Use only a sourced status; omit it for ordinary printings.


Optional '''set_icon''' — printed expansion symbol. Always shown. Premiere = none (still shown). Pass <code>none</code> or a wikilink/file for the printed icon. Alias '''expansion_icon'''. When omitted, Premiere-family sets (Premiere Limited, Premiere Unlimited, Premiere Two-Player, Premiere Two-Player Introductory Game, Premiere, Japanese Premiere, Japanese Premiere Two-Player, ESB Two-Player) default to <code>none</code>; other sets show an empty cell until filled. Do not mass-restamp 24k articles.

Optional '''also_in''' (alias '''products''') — leftover or extra products that shipped this same version (Enhanced Premiere boosters, First Anthology starters, Reflections I–III bulk). Named editions of the same cardboard stack in the article title instead. Omit when none.

Optional '''publisher''' — publisher credited by the set article (<code>[[Decipher]]</code>, <code>[[Players Committee]]</code>, or a named person). Inherit from the set infobox. For a cancelled set, use its documented planned publisher; this does not imply that the cards were released. Renders after Also in when filled.

Optional '''era''' — championship era hub: <code>[[Decipher era]]</code>, <code>[[Virtual Original]]</code>, <code>[[Virtual Legacy]]</code>, or <code>[[Virtual Modern]]</code>. Renders after Publisher when filled.

'''GEMP ID''' — the id GEMP actually loads, as <code>set_card</code> (for example <code>1220_51</code>, <code>1_19</code>). Bare on the current playable article, <code>o</code> on the first-published face, <code>d</code> only as a middle layer when print, Decipher errata, and PC errata are three distinct texts. Pass '''gemp_id''' or the older '''card_uid''' (alias). Optional '''gemp_id2''' — a second GEMP id when this version is a named edition of two constructed sets. Render both as adjacent <code><nowiki><code></nowiki></code> spans, 2PG first ('''gemp_id''') then Unlimited ('''gemp_id2'''). Omit '''gemp_id2''' when empty. Worked: Imperial Barrier white <code>71_249</code> then <code>51_249</code>. Shown in monospace. Dest keys such as <code>pc|vbN|...</code> belong in authoring JSON, not here.

Infobox identity order: Set, Set icon, Also in, Publisher, Era, GEMP ID, then rarity/stats/gameplay Icons.

Optional '''rarity''' and '''uniqueness''' — omit either field when the source does not establish it; no blank row is shown. Read uniqueness from the printed title marker: one bullet is Unique, no marker is Unrestricted, and multiple bullets use the corresponding Limited or Restricted value. For a combo, inspect the marker on both halves. If the title area is cropped or unreadable, omit uniqueness.

Optional '''credits''' — count only the gold coin circles in the card’s bottom credit area, following the card’s orientation. The single gold badge beside the lore panel is not a credit. Show only positive Credits. Omit the parameter when there are no credit coins or the value is unknown; empty, null and zero values do not render a row. Keep confirmed zero distinct from unknown in the source-data ledger.

Optional '''pc_alias''' — Players Committee GEMP alias (<code>601_x</code> / <code>501_x</code>) when it differs from the GEMP ID.

Optional '''slip''' — printed slip number on the virtual sheet (for example <code>51E</code>). Data, not the id.

'''Versions''' — family navigator (Option C, 26 October 2026; errata prefix 26 October 2026). Closed prefixes, oldest first: Decipher, Decipher (AI), Decipher Errata, PC Errata, Virtual Original, Virtual Legacy, Virtual Legacy (AI), Virtual Modern, Virtual Modern (ALT). Unmarked Decipher is the printed face. Decipher Errata is a later Decipher rewrite. PC Errata only when the Players Committee rewrote past Decipher. Full lineage both directions. Omit when this printing is the only one. Host twins that share one GEMP id use one line plus a hatnote. Pass '''versions''' or the older '''printings''' (alias). Bold the current-printing label and place its GEMP ID in <code><nowiki><code></nowiki></code>. Worked: [[Luke Skywalker]].

Do not pass '''version_label'''. The old Version row (printed / virtual) is dropped. Era and Versions already mark Players Committee printings as Virtual Original, Virtual Legacy, or Virtual Modern.

Optional '''version_code''' (Bill, 2026-11-08) — this page's errata version: <code>&lt;Issuer&gt;-E&lt;n&gt;</code>, where the issuer is <code>D</code> (Decipher) or <code>PC</code> (Players Committee) and n counts that card's published changes in date order, rephrases included (<code>PC-E1</code>, <code>PC-E2</code>…). Renders as '''Errata version''' above the Errata mark. Omit it on the original printed face, which has no code. It is our version id, not a printed stamp: the stamp printed on the card goes in '''errata_mark''' as printed (E1, D-E1). Page titles stay as in the Style guide: plain = original, then (Errata), (Errata 2), (Errata 3). Worked: [[Hindsight (V) (Errata)]] = <code>PC-E1</code>.


Optional '''likeness''' — person whose face is on the card: a photographic model Decipher (or the Players Committee) cast, or the film portrayer of that character. Wiki-link the person page. Worked: [[Mara Jade, The Emperor's Hand]] → [[Shannon Baksa]]; [[Aurra Sing]] / [[Aurra Sing (AI)]] → [[Michonne Bourriague]]. Omit when the art is illustration, a starship/weapon, or a later virtual photograph that is not that person.

Optional PC label fields (swccg-guild/work#100) — the small labels the Players Committee prints on a Virtual card, copied by bot from billbisco/swccg-gemp <code>card_labels.json</code>; correct them there, not here, or the next bot run puts the old value back. '''original_title''' — the black title strip at the bottom left (the title of the card this one was made from; on Virtual Legacy cards the slip title). '''original_title_italic''' — <code>yes</code> when the whole strip is italic, or the italic part (for example <code>Executor</code>). '''errata_mark''' — the errata stamp, bottom right (E1, D-E1). '''ai_mark''' — the alternate-image stamp as printed, (AI) or (ALT). '''concept_credit''' — the "Original concept by …" line. '''art_credit''' — the art credit printed beside the art ("Image courtesy of …"). '''dedication''' — an "In memory of …" line in the bottom bar. '''printed_label''' — any other small printed line (for example a contest name on the card's edge). '''copyright_line''' — the vertical copyright line beside the art, as printed (the standard "ARTWORK NEITHER AFFILIATED WITH NOR ENDORSED BY LUCASFILM LTD." too; Virtual Block lines are recorded only where legible). The '''Alternate-image stamp''' row shows the Players Committee logo printed beside (AI)/(ALT). Worked: [[Endless Legions]] (original title, concept and art credits); [[Executor: Control Station (V)]] (partly italic title, Decipher copyright line). All are omitted when the card doesn't print them.

Optional '''reviews''' — published reviews of this card (fan-site or magazine), one bullet each: reviewer, outlet, date when known, rating if given, a short summary and a brief quote, cited with a <code><nowiki><ref></nowiki></code> carrying the Preserved copy (set '''has_refs'''). Renders as '''Reviews''' after Strategy. Omit when none. Worked: [[Chasm]] (Jeff Hansen, Neglected Card Series).

Optional '''anagram''' — one sentence that the printed title is an anagram of a named person. Renders as '''Anagram'''. Adds [[:Category:Anagrams]]. Omit when none. Link [[Anagrams]] from See also. Worked: [[Nabrun Leids]] → [[Tom Braunlich]].

Optional '''joke''' — a joke in this printing's title, lore or game text, cited (or approved by Bill, with the approval on the card's Talk page). Renders as '''Joke''' directly after '''Anagram'''. Adds [[:Category:Jokes]]. Omit when none. Link [[Jokes]] from See also. Worked: [[Swing-And-A-Miss]].

Optional '''easter_egg''' — the hidden picture, icon, likeness or other visual detail on this printing, cited. Renders as '''Easter egg''' immediately before See Also. Adds [[:Category:Easter eggs]]. Omit when none. Link [[Easter eggs]] from See also. Worked: [[Death Star: Trench]].

'''sources''' — card-data sources supplied here (card list, slip, PDF). Give each source its own bullet with a Preserved copy. The template renders a '''Sources''' heading only when filled. Do not repeat a source already cited with <code><nowiki><ref></nowiki></code> for one claim. List it here again only when it supplies the entire card entry. '''has_refs''' — set when the page has <code><nowiki><ref></nowiki></code> notes; renders '''References'''. '''see_also''' renders '''See Also''' only when filled.

Optional '''image2''' — second portrait under '''image''' (same 280px width). Used for Objective 0/7 faces; omit on single-face cards.

Optional '''image2_trim''' — display-only trim for excess padding on the second image. A value of <code>20</code> requests a 320px thumbnail and hides 20px on each edge inside a 280px-wide rounded window. Measure each image separately and preserve a normal black border, all text and all symbols. The source File and downloaded image are unchanged. Omit for ordinary images.

Optional '''image2_layout''' — how to place '''image2''' when set:
* omit or '''stack''' — force stacked vertically (0 on top, 7 below); default when unset
* '''right''' — force side-by-side always (0 left, 7 right); classes '''card-portraits-row''' + '''card-rail-dual'''
* '''responsive''' — preferred Objective mode: wide viewport = side-by-side (0 left, 7 right); narrow viewport (max-width '''720px''') = stacked. Same row/dual markup plus '''card-rail-responsive''' / '''card-portraits-responsive''' so CSS media query can adapt.

Optional '''image3''', '''image4''', '''image5''', '''image6''' — further portraits, each 280px wide, with matching '''image3_trim''' … '''image6_trim''' (same rule as '''image2_trim'''). Used for the printed slip on [[Virtual Legacy]] card pages (swccg-guild/work#156), as '''image2''' shows the slip on [[Virtual Original]] pages.
* Stacked layout (no '''image2_layout'''): they follow '''image2''' in order, top to bottom. A single-face card whose '''image2''' is free puts its slip in '''image2'''; a card whose '''image2''' is taken puts the slip in '''image3''' (a slip printed in two halves uses the next free slots, top half first).
* '''right''' / '''responsive''' layout (two-sided Objectives): when '''image3''' or '''image4''' is set the portraits form two columns. The left column is '''image''' (0 side), '''image3''', '''image5'''; the right column is '''image2''' (7 side), '''image4''', '''image6'''. Put the 0 side's slip in '''image3''' and the 7 side's in '''image4'''; when a side's slip is printed in two halves, its second half goes in '''image5''' (0 side) or '''image6''' (7 side). In narrow (responsive) view the left column stacks above the right. Without '''image3'''/'''image4''' the layout is unchanged.

== Creature statistics ==

Optional creature statistics: <code>ferocity</code> and <code>fangs</code> render their own Info rows when supplied. Use the printed creature statistics rather than recording ferocity as power.

The optional <code>tentacles</code> parameter displays a creature’s printed tentacle count. Like <code>ferocity</code> and <code>fangs</code>, the row is omitted when the parameter is empty.

== Blanked date (Bill, 10 November 2026) ==
Optional '''blanked''' — the date the Players Committee blanked the card (in effect banned it), with a <code><nowiki><ref></nowiki></code> to the announcement, e.g. <code><nowiki>|blanked=26 April 2011<ref name="...">...</ref></nowiki></code>. It shows a ''Blanked'' row after ''Era'' and adds [[:Category:Blanked cards]]. Blanking is not a new version: the card stays in its set and is legal in period formats before that date. Leave it out on cards that were never blanked (no row is shown).

== Language and printing metadata ==

Optional '''language''' — ISO language code for this printing, for example <code>ja</code>. Shows the printed-language row and enables optional edition metadata. Omit for existing English entries. '''language_display''' supplies a sourced display value instead of the language name; '''label_language''' preserves an existing row label.

'''printed_title''', '''printed_game_text''' and '''printed_lore''' hold the printing's native text, including its punctuation and title markers. They render in their own language-tagged sections. '''translation''' holds the English translation separately; '''translation_note''' holds a comparison with the English printing. Never substitute English card text for an unreadable Japanese face. Preserve a distinction between a blank printed field and a field that has not been transcribed.

Optional '''edition''', '''border_finish''', '''release''', '''size''' and '''year''' show metadata rows when supplied together with '''language'''. Set identifies the product; '''set_icon''' identifies the symbol actually printed on this face. A foil or introductory product can reuse another expansion's symbol or print the premium symbol. Read the face rather than inferring its symbol from the product name.

The migration also supports existing article material through '''lead''', '''navigation''', '''image_note''', '''type_display''', '''set_display''', '''rarity_display''', '''extra_info''', '''extra_sections''' and '''see_also_heading'''. Display overrides preserve existing linked wording without changing the underlying side/type/set values. '''extra_info''' accepts table rows inside the shared infobox; it must not contain another infobox table. The '''label_type''', '''label_gemp_id''', '''label_dark_icons''', '''label_light_icons''', '''label_icons''', '''label_landspeed''' and '''label_versions''' overrides retain existing field labels. '''category_override''' retains an exceptional printing's complete existing category list; omit it for ordinary new entries.

Example of separate native and translated fields (an abridged language-field example; add the verified image, statistics, Versions and sources for a complete article):
<pre>
{{Card
|title=Alderaan
|side=Light
|type=Location
|subtype=System
|set=Premiere (Japanese)
|language=ja
|set_icon=None ([[Premiere Limited|Premiere]])
|printed_title=オルデラン
|translation='''Title:''' Alderaan.
}}
</pre>

== Source-photo orientation ==

Optional '''image_rotation''' — <code>left</code> displays the first portrait a quarter turn counterclockwise. Use it for an original source photograph whose card is sideways. The original File and downloaded photograph stay unchanged. Omit it for an upright photo. '''image_rotated_height''' is the displayed height in pixels after rotation; use the nearest integer to <code>280 × original image width / original image height</code> (default 167). The template scales the standard thumbnail inside its 280px rail. Works with the first portrait in stacked and two-column layouts. Do not use rotation to infer a different printing or to hide a cropped card edge.
